thesis: In the supplied 128-node synthetic stencil workload scenario, coordinating incremental checkpoints reduced measured checkpoint interruption while preserving recovery coverage.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.goal: Establish the checkpoint-interruption problem for large HPC applications, introduce the bounded central claim, and state the paper's contribution within the closed-world fixture scenario.

sections.title: Background: Checkpointing in HPC Systems
sections.goal: Provide the two background examples (full-checkpoint and incremental-checkpoint approaches) sufficient for a systems researcher to understand the coordination design, without external citations.

sections.title: Checkpoint Coordinator Design
sections.goal: Describe the coordination mechanism for incremental checkpoints: scheduling policy, state tracking, and recovery-coverage preservation invariant.

sections.title: Fixture Evidence: Measured Interruption and Recovery
sections.goal: Present the closed-world benchmark observations (128 nodes, 8 trials per configuration, baseline 41.2 s vs coordinated 27.8 s mean interruption, all recovery checks passed) with explicit fixture limitations.

sections.title: Discussion: Interpretation and Limitations
sections.goal: Interpret the interruption reduction strictly within the supplied scenario, state fixture limitations (no variance, no CIs, no raw values, no other workloads), and address the alternative explanation that the result is a scenario artifact.

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.goal: Restate the bounded contribution, summarize what the fixture evidence does and does not support, and identify the deferred external-literature work as a future direction.
